ig_caption:
Bidirectional A* on Real Maps: The Ultimate Pathfinding Algorithm — how routing AI finds the fastest path in milliseconds ⚡

Imagine two A* searches working in parallel:
1) Forward A* expands from your start node using g(n)+h(n).
2) Backward A* expands from the goal node using gᵣ(n)+hᵣ(n).
3) When the frontiers meet, we stitch the route together with the best combined cost.

Why it’s fast:
• Less explored area than classic A* (bidirectional cuts the “blast radius”).
• Heuristics (h) guide both searches, but correctness depends on consistent assumptions.
• In road networks (like GPS routing), fewer node expansions = quicker re-planning.

Takeaway: Bidirectional A* is a graph search strategy that treats the map like a weighted network and computes an optimal (or near-optimal) route by meeting-in-the-middle.

Debate: Should autonomous vehicles always prefer bidirectional search for speed—or prioritize safer routing with additional constraints (turn costs, traffic, risk) instead?
